definition: An objective indicator is a measurable sign from a test that assesses a bodily function without relying on subjective judgment. In this packet, it refers to evidence of normally functioning outer hair cells in the cochlea.

provenance.scope: Source record C184951; pinned source text

reasons: The packet supports that distortion-product otoacoustic emissions are an objective indicator of normally functioning cochlear outer hair cells, but it does not explicitly support the broader gloss that an objective indicator is a measurable sign from a test that assesses bodily function without relying on subjective judgment.
The definition slightly generalizes beyond the packet by presenting a general definition of the term rather than the packet-specific sense only.
The definition’s first sentence gives a general characterization (“measurable sign… without relying on subjective judgment”) that is not stated in the packet.

The packet specifically ties “objective indicator” to distortion-product otoacoustic emissions being an objective indicator of normally functioning cochlear outer hair cells, but it does not support the broader general description in the definition’s first sentence.
